title: Technical QA Engineer (Laravel + Vue 2, post-deploy), EU property-tech + SaaS, remote
description:
Role

We ship small changes to our live platforms often. We want a technical QA engineer with a real developer background: you think like a user, but you can also read the code path, review merge requests, and tell us when the fix or the AI-suggested change should be different. After each release you check that landlords, renters, candidates and companies can still get from A to B to C. You are not the person who builds features full time, but you are close to a half-developer on our stack. Speed and quality, not one at the cost of the other.



About us

We are a European property-tech company. We run several live rental and property platforms on one shared Laravel and Vue 2 codebase, plus a recruitment SaaS where candidates record video intakes for companies and agencies. We use GitLab merge requests. We care about security, privacy, and small reviewable changes.



Where you sit in our flow

We roll out to production often and we want to keep that pace. Developers deploy; you are not a gate before release and you do not own the deploy button. After each production rollout you test on
 the journeys that release touched, then the critical paths users depend on, on desktop and mobile, with test accounts and safe paths where we need them. You are the second check after go-live, not a blocker in front of it. When something fails for a real user, you report it fast with steps, expected versus actual, and enough detail that a developer can fix it the same day.



How we work

Our developers work with AI coding assistants and keep their changes small. You test the outcome in the browser and you sanity-check the change in GitLab: read the diff, spot risky patterns, and push back when generated code is sloppy or the wrong layer was touched. If something works on paper but feels wrong in the browser, you say so. You may use AI tools yourself, but the pass or fail comes from what you verified, not from what the model claimed.



What you will do

- After each production rollout, smoke-test the journeys that release touched, on desktop and on mobile

- Re-run the critical journeys per product: listing a property, booking a viewing, uploading documents, recording a video intake, reviewing candidates

- Explore beyond the release note when something looks fragile

- Check that a change on one platform did not break or leak into another platform on the same codebase

- Write clear bug reports: steps to reproduce, expected versus actual, severity, environment, browser and device, screenshot or short video

- Point developers to the file, layer, or request: Blade, Vue component, controller, query, or API response

- Give UX feedback in plain words, for example "a landlord would not know what to do here"

- Review merge requests and recent commits: what changed, what could regress, what should have been tested, what you would do differently

- Suggest concrete improvements to developers (and to AI-generated patches): safer query, clearer validation, better error handling, smaller scope



Requirements

- Strong technical background: you have worked as a developer or as QA embedded with developers, and you can read Laravel and Vue 2 code in a real codebase, not only tutorials

- Hands-on experience with Laravel web applications and Vue 2 front ends in production, or equivalent depth with a similar PHP plus SPA stack and a clear plan to work in our Vue 2 patterns

- Experience with multi-brand or multi-tenant products: one codebase, several sites or customers, and you know how a fix on one brand can break another

- Proven QA on live web products, with examples where your report or your review caught something others missed

- You think in user journeys and in the people behind them

- Clear written English, short and precise

- Solid GitLab or GitHub habits: branches, merge requests, reading diffs, commenting on specific lines

- Browser developer tools: console, network tab, status codes; you tie UI symptoms to backend responses

- Comfortable challenging AI-assisted development: you review output like a senior teammate, not like a checklist-only tester

- Reliable and self-directed: you find the next useful check without being told

- This role is QA and review first. We do not hire you primarily to ship features. Occasional tiny fixes are a bonus, not the job description.



Nice to have

- Accessibility basics: keyboard use, contrast, readable forms

- Ideas for light automated checks or regression notes, without making automation the whole role

- Docker-based local setup or Laravel Mix familiarity



Working hours: full time, 40 hours a week, Monday to Friday, 09:00 to 17:00 Amsterdam time. That is 15:00 to 23:00 in the Philippines in European summer, and 16:00 to 00:00 when Europe switches to winter time. Please state your timezone and the window you can reliably cover each workday.



Paid trial (before full engagement)

A paid trial week of about five working days, full time, at $3 per hour, tracked with TimeProof after signing. We give you test accounts, a short list of recent rollouts to verify the same way you would after go-live, and read-only visibility on merge requests where useful. You test like a real user on desktop and mobile, file bug reports and UX notes, and add technical review comments where you see risk in the change. You may use AI tools, but you must not paste secrets, customer data, production logs, or private business information into external tools. You must be able to explain and defend everything you report and every review comment.



The deal

Remote, full time, long term. Hours are tracked with TimeProof. Rate: $3 per hour to start, reviewed on quality and impact. This is a long-term role, not a one-off project.



How to apply (English, no template letters)

1) Start your message with ABC.

2) One bug you found in production that others missed: how you reproduced it and how you reported it.

3) How you would test a release right after it goes live, without slowing every release down.

4) One example of UX feedback you gave that changed a flow.

5) A form submits and nothing happens. What do you send the developer?

6) One merge request or diff you reviewed: what you looked at in the code, what you worried about, and what you asked the developer to change.

7) Your timezone and the Amsterdam-time window you can cover.



Keep it short. Selected applicants do a short video intake on our platform before we talk.



Do not apply if

- You are not the person who will do the work

- You only know QA in theory and cannot give real examples

- You have never read application code or merge request diffs in a real job

- You only write automated tests and do not think about the people using the product

- You want a pure development role with no testing responsibility

- You cannot write clear English

- You would paste secrets, production logs, or customer data into external tools

- That means working at the level of APIs, your own scripts, and your own automations, not clicking together a stack of expensive closed services.

- You build it once, we own it, and it keeps paying off across every channel and every country.



What you will do (the core)

- Build AI-powered, multi-channel outreach that we own and that scales worldwide, market by market:
 at volume, AI calling, social, and WhatsApp where it fits.

- For the property platform: reach real estate agents in every market and bring them onto the platform, listing their properties and getting viewings booked. The AI calls and messages carry one clear call to action: visit the site and get started.

- For the SaaS: reach staffing and recruitment agencies and get them on board and active in the same way.

- It is one engine for both products. You build it once and it runs for property and for staffing, country by country.

- Make it work in any language. Build a reliable localization approach so the outreach reads native in each market, using AI translation with quality control and native review where it matters. Rough machine translation does not cut it; the message has to feel local, not foreign.

- Drive social amplification: get agents and agencies to follow, like, and share our content, so reach compounds.

- Build the lead data, sequences, and automations yourself, and keep them deliverable and legal in every market you touch: GDPR in Europe, anti-spam laws such as CAN-SPAM, and local rules on
 and automated calling. Warmed domains, clear opt-out, and consent where it is required. Compliance and deliverability are part of the job, not an afterthought.

- Measure everything: replies, signups, activations, and double down on what works.



What you will do (the bonus, all-round)

- Content and social management, basic SEO, paid campaigns, simple design, reporting.



How you build it (we like builders, not renters)

- Comfortable wiring up LLM APIs (OpenAI, Anthropic) in your own workflows.

- Comfortable with self-hostable automation (for example n8n) and your own scripts over closed SaaS where it makes sense.

- Can build your own lead data, localization, and outreach pipeline instead of depending on one paid platform.

- For AI calling, you wire telephony and voice models yourself rather than relying on a closed black box.

If you already build your own automations instead of renting them, tell us. That is exactly who we want.



Who you are

- You think in systems and you build and own them.

- You have grown something real and can show it, with a number.

- You are comfortable with volume, testing, and iteration.

- You write clear English, and you have a proven way to make outreach read natively in many other languages (AI localization with quality control, native review where it matters). You do not rely on rough machine translation.

- You respect the law in each country you reach into, and you treat compliance as part of doing it well, not a brake. You know that automated calling in particular is tightly regulated and you handle it carefully, market by market.

- You are self-starting and reliable, and you keep brands safe (no spammy shortcuts that get domains blacklisted).



The deal

- Remote, full-time preferred. We start at a fair entry rate and raise it quickly for people who prove results.

- We test with a small paid task first, then move fast for the right person.

- As we scale this across both products and more markets, there is room for it to grow into more than one role.



How to apply (please read)

1. Start your message with the word GROWTH so I know you read this.

2. In a few lines, answer this: how would you reach 10,000 real estate agents in one country using AI, end to end, how would you keep it legal and deliverable there (think GDPR, anti-spam, and rules on automated calling), how would you make the outreach read natively in that country's language, and which parts would you build yourself versus rent?

3. Add one example of something you have grown, with a number.

Applications that skip these get less attention. We reply to serious ones quickly.

title: AI-Augmented Laravel + Vue 2 Developer / Engineer (EU property/SaaS-tech, remote)
description:
Role

We are looking for a strong, reliable engineer who likes to move fast with AI tools and still ships carefully. We care heavily about clear communication, good decisions, and a clean trial result.



About us

We are a European property-tech company. We maintain a long-running Laravel application with Blade, Vue 2, Bootstrap, and tenant-scoped data patterns. We use GitLab merge requests. We care about security, privacy, and small reviewable changes.



How we work

We use an AI-assisted development workflow. You are expected to use coding assistants to speed up analysis and implementation, but you treat generated output as draft work: clarify scope, plan the change, verify behaviour, keep diffs small, and prove changes with sensible and thorough checks and testing before review.



This role is a great fit if you like turning requirements into a short plan, using AI where it helps, keeping changes easy to review, and checking your work before you ask for feedback. It is not a fit if you want to ship large unreviewed blocks of AI-generated code.



What you will do

- Deliver scoped changes on a mature Laravel + Vue 2 codebase using AI-assisted methods safely.

- Open merge requests with clear descriptions, scoped commits, and tests where applicable.

- Communicate in writing about plan, trade-offs, and verification steps.



Requirements

- Demonstrable AI-assisted workflow in real product work (you can explain it concretely).

- Comfortable working in Laravel in a larger codebase, including reading and navigating existing code you did not write yourself.

- Comfortable with Vue 2 in production, or strong Vue experience with a clear plan to work within Vue 2 patterns in this codebase.

- Comfortable with Blade templates and web security (escaping, CSRF, safe handling of user input).

- Solid Git habits: branches, scoped commits, merge request workflow.

- Written English strong enough for async work with EU stakeholders.

- Ideally 4 to 6 hours overlap per workday with CET business hours (Monday to Friday). Please state your timezone and the CET window you can reliably cover each workday.



Nice to have

- AI-assisted work on legacy codebases (careful refactors, incremental upgrades, tenant-scoped features).

- Laravel Mix / Webpack and Docker-based local builds.

- Multi-tenant SaaS experience.



Trial (before any production access)

We run a mini-trial on a sandbox repository that mirrors our stack patterns but contains no production code or customer data. Timebox is about 4 to 6 hours, agreed upfront.



You may use AI tools during the trial, but you must not paste secrets, customer data, production logs, or private business information into external tools. You must be able to explain and defend everything you submit.



How to apply (English, no template letters)

1) Your current AI-assisted workflow: how you scope prompts, verify output, and prevent scope creep.

2) One example where an AI tool gave a wrong or risky suggestion. How did you catch it?

3) Either (A) walk us through one concrete merge request or commit you authored where AI was your primary tool: what you prompted, what came back, and what you changed before merge, or (B) if you cannot share a link, describe your first 30 minutes on an unfamiliar legacy Laravel/Vue task before you edit code.

4) How do you keep AI-assisted changes small and reviewable in a legacy monolith?

5) Multi-tenant safety: what checks would you do before changing a query that returns tenant-owned records?

6) What information must never be pasted into external AI tools? Name categories, not examples from real projects.



Do not apply if

- You are not the person who will do the work.

- You ship AI output without verification.

- You cannot describe your workflow concretely.

- You only have Vue 3 experience and cannot commit to Vue 2 patterns in this codebase.

- You would paste secrets, production logs, or customer data into external tools.

title: General Virtual Assistant  (Admin, Social Media & Video Editing)
description:
We're looking for a reliable, organised, and detail-oriented General Virtual Assistant to support two growing businesses: Locals in the Loop and ABC Digital.



The main priority for this role is reliability and consistency. We need someone who takes ownership of their work, pays attention to detail, meets deadlines, and can be trusted to complete recurring tasks without constant follow-ups.



If you're proactive, organised, and confident in administration, Canva, and video editing, we'd love to hear from you!



Responsibilities



Handle weekly data entry for the Locals in the Loop gig guide (approximately 8 hours per week).



Provide general administrative support across both businesses.



Create graphics using existing Canva templates.



Edit reels and short-form videos for Locals in the Loop and ABC Digital clients.



Assist with social media management for clients in hospitality, gyms, breweries, and short-stay accommodation.



Support
 campaigns and ManyChat automations as the role grows.



Ensure tasks are completed accurately and consistently within agreed deadlines.



Requirements



Proven reliability and a strong track record of showing up and meeting deadlines.



Excellent attention to detail, particularly with data entry.



Confident using Canva for template-based graphics.



Experience editing videos using Filmora or Adobe Premiere Pro. CapCut experience alone will not meet this requirement.



Strong written English and communication skills.



Ability to follow instructions, manage recurring tasks, and work independently.



Availability to work the required fixed hours.



Nice to Have



Experience with ManyChat.



Experience creating and managing
 campaigns.



Social media experience with hospitality, venues, or events brands.



Previous experience working with Australian businesses.



How to Apply



If you're interested in this position, please
 
 with the following:



 subject: Gen VA ABC – [Your Name]



Please include:



Summary of experience: A brief introduction outlining your relevant experience in administration, data entry, Canva, and video editing.



CV/Resume: Attach your updated CV.



Portfolio: Include examples of your Canva designs and video editing work, if available.



WhatsApp number: Provide your active WhatsApp number for faster communication.



Only shortlisted applicants will be contacted via WhatsApp.



We're looking for someone dependable who takes pride in their work, communicates well, and is interested in building a long-term working relationship with the team.



If this sounds like you, we look forward to receiving your application!

title: VIDEO EDITOR – DTC BEAUTY & PERSONAL CARE
description:
We are looking for a Video Editor to help scale the performance creative engine of a fast-growing DTC beauty & personal care brand primarily serving the US market.



This role is responsible for turning creative briefs into high-performing video ads across Meta and TikTok, including UGC ads, product demonstrations, AI-generated creatives, iterations of winning concepts, and new creative experiments.



We are looking for someone who understands direct-response advertising, consumer psychology, and performance creative — not just video editing.



KEY RESPONSIBILITIES



• Edit high-performing video ads based on creative briefs, including UGC, product demos, storytelling ads, and AI-generated creatives

• Collaborate closely with Creative Strategists to turn concepts, hooks, and scripts into engaging performance assets

• Create iterations of winning ads by improving hooks, pacing, visuals, storytelling, and overall execution based on performance insights

• Develop AI-generated video content using tools such as AI avatars, AI scenes, AI animation, voiceovers, and AI-assisted editing workflows

• Maintain strong visual quality, brand consistency, and alignment with the creative strategy

• Continuously improve editing workflows to increase creative testing speed and output quality



REQUIREMENTS



• Proven experience editing performance ads for DTC brands

• Experience in beauty, skincare, cosmetics, wellness, or personal care is a strong plus

• Strong understanding of Meta and TikTok advertising formats and what makes ads convert

• Experience using AI-generated content and AI creative tools

• Ability to understand a creative brief and independently translate strategy into compelling visuals

• Strong attention to detail in pacing, storytelling, shot selection, visual logic, and overall ad quality

• Comfortable working in a fast-paced environment with frequent creative iterations



HOW TO APPLY



Please include the following in your application:



1. Your portfolio link and CV

2. Have you worked with any beauty, skincare, cosmetics, wellness, or personal care brands? If so, please specify the brand names and specify your role and length of experience.

4. Your current availability/start date

5. Your expected monthly salary

6. A short note on the editing tools and AI tools you use

7. From a clear brief and provided raw footage, how many finished 30–60 second ad can you normally produce in one day?

8. For a 1-minute video, how long does it usually take you to re-edit the video after receiving revision feedback?

9. How many years have you been a full-time video editor?

10. Which types of performance ad creatives are you strongest at editing, and which are you less confident with? Please list them separately (e.g., UGC, product demos, testimonials, storytelling ads, AI-generated creatives etc).

11. Are you currently working with any other clients or companies? Looking for fractional or full-time?



Applications that do not follow the requested format may not be considered.

title: Customer support assistant
description:
Read this entire post before applying. If you skim it, you will fail the application in the first five seconds and we will both have wasted our time. That is not a threat — it's a favor. This job is not for most people, and I'd rather you find that out now.





WHAT THIS JOB ACTUALLY IS

We are a Swedish e-commerce company running several brands. Every brand gets customer
s every day, and every one of them needs a correct answer the same day. Forever.



Your job: clear the support inboxes every day. Different brands, different languages, the same questions over and over:



"Where is my delivery?"

Order not received.

Product not as expected.

Returns and exchanges.

General questions about the brand.



The
s are boring. The job is not. Here is what a normal day actually looks like:



Open the inboxes. Look each order up in Shopify. Find the tracking. Reply in the customer's language using DeepL, following our reply guide.

When tracking has been dead for a week, you do not tell the customer "please wait." You message our shipping agents in China, get an answer, and then tell the customer what is actually happening and when.

When a customer opens a dispute with their bank, you collect the evidence — order, tracking, delivery proof, your
 thread — and submit it to the payment provider. Before the deadline. Without being reminded.

When the same problem shows up three times in one week, you write it down and tell us. Once, with numbers.



The tools: Shopify admin,
, DeepL, the carriers' tracking pages, the payment provider's dispute portal, and a chat with our China agents. We teach you all of it in week one.





THE ONE THING THIS JOB IS REALLY ABOUT

We are in Sweden and we spend our days running ads. We are not going to sit next to you. If you message us "what should I do?" three times a day, this job has failed — for both of us.



The rule is simple. Before anything reaches us, you have already tried to solve it. When it still has to reach us, it arrives like this — four lines, nothing else:



The problem: Order 4471, tracking dead for 11 days, customer threatening a chargeback.

What I already did: Checked the carrier page, asked the China agent on Monday and again on Wednesday, no reply.

What I propose: Offer a replacement now, refund only if there is no scan by Friday.

What I need from you: A yes or a no.



That is the whole job in four lines. Anyone can answer "where is my order" when the tracking works. I am hiring the person who knows what to do when it doesn't — and who d
 first and asks second.



Quick question, and I mean it: a customer writes in Danish, and DeepL is down for the whole day. What do you do? Put your answer on the very last line of your application, after everything else. You'll see why below.





WHAT WE ACTUALLY CARE ABOUT, IN THIS EXACT ORDER

1. You show up. Every single day, Saturday and Sunday included. Not "most days." Not "I had internet problems." Every day.

2. The inbox is cleared inside your window, every day. Nothing sits for more than 24 hours without a reply.

3. You d
 first and ask second. Every time something reaches us, it comes with your proposed solution.

4. You stay. We are building a team, not renting an assistant for two months.

5. Your English and your tone are good enough — and get better.



Notice that skill is fifth on this list. That is not a mistake. We can teach you our brands, our reply guide, our shipping, our tone — we have a whole system for it, and the person who reads this carefully and types "kanelbulle" as the first word of the subject line when applying is already showing me the exact trait I'm hiring for. It is not mentioned in the subject line structure below, but it is supposed to be the first word, then the structure. What we cannot teach is a person who opens the inbox every single day for the next two years, weekends included, and who would rather make a decision than wait for one.





HOURS — READ THIS PART HONESTLY

This is work on demand. There is no fixed shift. The rule is simple: the inbox is cleared every day, 7 days a week, inside 10:00–17:00 Swedish time. If you are in the Philippines, that window is 17:00–00:00 right now (16:00–23:00 in summer). You d
 when inside it. The workload has grown fast: right now the job takes several hours every day, and it keeps growing as we add brands and tasks. Weekends are never optional.



You log the hours you actually work, and you are paid for them. More hours come with more brands and more tasks.



If you cannot open the inbox every single day, including weekends, do not apply. That is the entire job.





PAY — READ THIS PART SLOWLY

Hourly rate, paid twice a month, on time, every time. We have never missed a payment and we never will.



The rate ladder, in writing:



Start: $2.50 USD per hour.

After 1 month: $3.00 USD per hour.

After 3 months: $3.50 USD per hour.

After 6 months: $4.00 USD per hour.



Every step is automatic if you are still clearing the inbox every day. It goes into your agreement on day one. You will never have to ask me for a raise, and I will never "forget." The first raise comes after ONE month. Not six. Not "we'll see." One month.



On top of that:



$20 USD consistency bonus every month you open the inbox on every single day with zero missed days. This is the easiest money in the job, and it is entirely within your control.

$3 USD per Trustpilot review. Every 4- or 5-star review from a real customer that mentions you by name. Uncapped, and this is the real upside. A customer who was angry on Monday and names you in a 5-star review on Thursday is exactly the job, and you get paid for it every time it happens. Each review is matched to a real order before it is paid.



One line on that, because it matters: you never ask a customer for a rating, you never offer a customer anything for a review, and you never write one yourself. One fake, bought or nudged review and the seat is gone the same day. The reviews you get paid for are the ones you earned by fixing the problem so well that the customer wanted to say your name.



You are paid for the hours you actually work, not for counting
s. Some days are calmer. Some days are a full inbox and a dispute deadline. Either way, the day is cleared.





WHAT COUNTS AS DONE

Every customer
 that arrived before 17:00 Swedish time is answered the same day, in the customer's language, following the reply guide, with the order looked up in Shopify. Every dispute is answered before its deadline. Anything that reaches us comes in the four-line format above. Not a taste judgment. If I send something back, I tell you exactly why in one sentence, and it counts once you fix it.





WHO SHOULD NOT APPLY

Please save us both the time. Do not apply if:



You cannot open the inbox every single day, Saturday and Sunday included.

Your internet is unreliable and you have no backup connection.

You have no plan for brownouts or power cuts.

You need someone to tell you what to do for each
.

You take angry customers personally, or argue with them.

You have never used Shopify admin. Not "seen it" — used it.

You want to negotiate the rate upward before you've proven a single month.

You are looking for a placeholder while you search for something better.

You want the "future tasks" at the bottom of this post to be the job now. They come after months of a cleared inbox, not before.



I'm not being harsh for fun. I'd rather describe the job exactly than lose a good person who wanted a different one.





HOW TO APPLY — THIS IS THE FIRST TEST

Ninety percent of applicants will get this wrong. That's the point.



1. Subject line, formatted EXACTLY like this:

| [most customer
s you have ever answered in ONE day] | [years using Shopify admin] | [hours/day you can work] | [days/week you can work] | [your download speed from speedtest.net]



Example: XXXXXX | 45 | 2 | 2 | 7 | 40mbps



Wrong format or a missing field — deleted unread. No exceptions, no second chances.



2. Your message must contain these eight things, in this order, and nothing else:



Line 1 — The most customer
s you have ever answered in a single day. For which store, and what kind of tickets. One or two real sentences. Generic answers are deleted.



Your setup — Computer and specs. Internet provider and speed. Backup internet. What you do when the power goes out. Be specific and boring. "I have good internet" is a failed answer.



Longevity — The longest you have ever stayed in one role or with one client. How long, and why it ended. Be honest. A short history with an honest reason beats an inflated one.



The reply — Reply to this customer in English, exactly as you would send it, maximum 120 words: "Hi, I ordered 12 days ago and nothing has arrived. Nobody answers. I want my money back." No order number was given, and you cannot find the customer by their
 address. Your reply is your portfolio.



The escalation — An order shipped from China 16 days ago. Tracking has said "in transit" for 9 days. The China agent has not answered for 48 hours. The customer says she will call her bank tomorrow. Write the message you would send me, in the four-line format from this post. Maximum 8 lines in total. If you write more than that, you have failed this part.



One honest answer — What would make you quit this job? Everyone has a breaking point. Tell me yours. I trust the person who names it far more than the person who says "nothing."



Shopify — The first thing you open in Shopify admin when a customer says the package hasn't arrived, and what you look at there.



Last line — The answer to the question I asked you earlier in this post. If it isn't there, you didn't read the post. If it is, I already know two things about you.



3. If I message you, reply within 24 hours. If you don't, I move on to the next applicant. Answering fast is part of the job, so it is part of the test.



Do not attach a generic CV. It will not be read.





THE THREE STAGES

Stage 1 — The application above. Takes 25 minutes if you're serious. Most people won't do it.



Stage 2 — The inbox test. Unpaid. If your application is sharp, I send you five real customer
s (names removed) in three languages, our reply guide, and access to DeepL. You return five replies within 24 hours. One of the five has no answer in the guide. I am watching what you do with that one: guess, ask a smart question, or find it. I am not grading style. I am grading: did you follow the guide exactly, did you deliver on time, and did you d
 before you asked. This is a real preview of the daily job.



Stage 3 — Paid trial week on one brand's live inbox. Real customers, real China agents, real feedback. This is where the seat is won.





WHAT YOU GET IF YOU WIN IT

One company, several brands, the same people every day. You choose when you work inside the window. Pay on time, twice a month, without ever having to ask. A rate that grows on a schedule you can see, and hours that grow with the work. Someone who tells you exactly what's wrong in one sentence so you can fix it and get better fast.



And a real path. Once the inbox has been cleared every day for months, the next tasks are real: finding products, searching for ad videos, writing ad copy, product descriptions, talking to UGC creators and influencers. We train you for them. But that comes after, not instead.



And the upside has no ceiling: every customer who names you in a 4- or 5-star review is $3 in your pocket, forever, on top of everything above.



If you're the kind of person who is tired of clients who never answer, and who just wants a seat, a standard to hit, and to be paid reliably for hitting it — this is that.



Show me you can follow instructions, and show me you can d
. That's the whole first test.

title: Customer Service Specialist – Strong Attention to Detail
description:
We're looking for a dependable, detail-oriented Customer Service Specialist to be the voice of our fashion brands. This is a long-term role for someone who writes well, stays calm under pressure, and takes ownership of a customer's issue from first message to resolution. You'll work independently, with AI tools supporting a large share of your replies.



What you'll do



- Handle the daily
 inbox — answering pre-sale questions, order status queries, complaints and escalations promptly and in a consistent brand voice (expected output: 30–40 tickets per hour with AI support).

- Own the full resolution, not just the reply: chase what's needed behind the scenes and close the loop with the customer.

Apply our return and refund policies confidently — offering discounts to retain a sale, issuing refunds, and sending clear return instructions.

- De-escalate unhappy customers and turn recoverable situations into repeat buyers.

- Resolve order issues around size, colour, stock availability and address verification before they become complaints, and follow up on unfulfilled Shopify orders.

- Report damaged or incorrect items to suppliers (via 
 or CJ Dropshipping) and secure replacements or refunds on the customer's behalf.

- Coordinate with suppliers on shipment updates, replacements and cancellations so you can give customers accurate answers, not guesses.

- Keep internal spreadsheets and documentation accurate so nothing falls through the cracks.

- Flag recurring complaint patterns and propose fixes — you're closest to the customer, so we want your input.



What we're looking for



-Proven customer service experience in e-commerce, ideally fashion (applications without this won't be reviewed).

-Excellent written English — clear, warm, and free of errors. This is the core of the job.

-Hands-on experience with helpdesk tools (HelpScout, Zendesk, Gorgias) and Shopify. Please add the word sky in the subject line of your application.

-Working knowledge of CJ Dropshipping order fulfilment — enough to chase a supplier and resolve an order yourself.

-Strong organisational skills and the ability to manage a busy queue independently.

-Analytical, detail-oriented, and comfortable proposing process improvements.



What we offer



Competitive salary + KPI-based bonuses

Long-term, fully remote setup

Part-time position that will potentially be absorbed as full time

Working hours would be around 9pm to 6am [Philippine Time]

Real growth opportunity as the company expands



To apply, send:

title: Operations Project Manager (Ecommerce)
description:
Operations Project Manager (Ecommerce): keeps SoFyre's ecommerce projects, partners and processes on track across Shopify, Amazon and TikTok Shop. Full-time, remote, work from home. Reports to the COO.

Your job is to make sure nothing falls through the cracks in our online business: every project has an owner, every task has a deadline, and every partner delivers.



You've run projects at an ecommerce or DTC brand before. You know how an online store works end to end: product launches, inventory and fulfillment, marketplaces, agencies and apps.



You're organised and direct. You follow up until things are done, and you're comfortable chasing team members, agencies, suppliers and warehouses alike.



You make processes simple. When something breaks, like a late shipment, a stockout or a listing issue, you find out why, fix it, and write down the new way so it sticks.



Your purpose at SoFyre is to be the COO's right hand, so that the team and partners hit their deadlines and the store runs smoothly as it grows.



PRIMARY ROLES

First 90 days:

- Learn how we work: our Shopify store, Amazon and TikTok Shop, Notion Ops HQ, our weekly rhythm, our partners and our SOP Hub

- Clean up Ops HQ so every task has one owner, a due date and a clear finish line

- Take over the Monday plan and Friday review

- Take over day-to-day follow-up with our main partners: warehouse, suppliers and agencies



Ongoing:

- Ops HQ: run projects and tasks in Notion, run the Monday plan and Friday review, and chase owners on overdue items

- Inventory and fulfillment follow-up: work with Supply Chain to keep POs, stock levels and shipments on schedule

- SOPs and process: write and update SOPs, find broken processes and fix them

- Tools and automation: lead new tool and AI rollouts with our AI Automation Engineer

- Flag risks and decisions that need the COO or CEO early, with the facts they need

- Post a daily status update

- Must have: 3+ years in project management or operations at an ecommerce or DTC brand

- Strong with Notion (or a similar tool), Google Sheets and Slack

- Has written SOPs or process guides

- Experience with remote teams across time zones

- Fluent written English



CHARACTER TRAITS

- Highly organised and reliable

- Follows up without being asked

- Clear, direct communicator

- Calm under pressure, especially during launches and peak season

- Takes ownership of misses

- Likes making things simpler

GROWTH POTENTIAL

With strong performance, growth paths include:

title: Instagram DM Setter, Part-Time (Online Fitness Coaching, Australia)
description:
About us

We're PhysiqLab 
 on Instagram, 27K+ followers), an Australian online fitness coaching business run by Jon and Jake. We help people lose fat, build muscle and stay consistent, with recipes and training our followers love.



The job

You'll message our new followers on Instagram, have friendly conversations about their fitness goals, and send a booking link to people who want help. Jon takes the call from there. You'll follow our proven scripts and Reply Playbook, and we'll train you step by step for 3 weeks. We also provide a Claude AI account set up to help you write replies.



Schedule

Monday to Friday + Sunday, 2:30pm to 7:00pm Philippines time. Saturday off.



Pay

- US$136 per week (A$195) base, paid weekly

- From week 4: +US$10 per booked call where the person stays for the full call, +US$35 per 12-week client, +US$70 per 24-week client

- Pay rise to US$160 per week (A$230) at 90 days if you hit your targets



You're right for this if you:

- Write excellent, casual, friendly English (not robotic or overly formal)

- Are reliable and on time for every shift

- Follow a checklist exactly, and ask when you're unsure

- Take feedback well

- Bonus: you're into fitness or nutrition, have done DM or appointment setting before, or are comfortable using AI tools like ChatGPT or Claude



How to apply (read carefully)

Start your application with the word PROTEIN. Applications without it won't be read. Then include:



1. Two or three sentences about you and any DM, sales or customer chat experience

2. One post 
 you liked, and why

3. Your replies to 4 real conversations. When someone follows us, we send them a friendly welcome message asking about their fitness goals. Here are four replies we've received. Write exactly what you'd send back to each one, in your own words. Please don't use AI for this part, we want to see how you write:

Please apply through OnlineJobs.ph only. Don't message our Instagram, as those messages won't be read.

title: Food Content Video Editor
description:
About the Role



We’re looking for a creative and detail-oriented Video Editor to transform food footage into engaging, high-quality videos for our food content platform.



You’ll work with our content team to produce visually appealing videos that showcase restaurant dishes, highlight their best features, and deliver an enjoyable viewing experience for our users.



Key Responsibilities



* Video Editing: Edit food videos into engaging, polished content suitable for our platform.

* Content Enhancement: Improve pacing, transitions, and visual presentation while ensuring the food remains the focus.

* Quality Control: Ensure videos meet established content standards, including proper framing, clean edges, smooth playback, and consistent quality.

* Following Editing Guidelines: Apply provided editing instructions, timestamps, and feedback accurately.

* Revisions: Make necessary adjustments based on feedback from the quality assurance team.

* Workflow Management: Organize completed videos and update their status to ensure an efficient production process.



Qualifications



* Experience in video editing, preferably for social media or short-form content.

* Familiarity with vertical video formats (9:16) and platforms such as Instagram Reels and TikTok.

* Proficiency in video editing software such as Adobe Premiere Pro, After Effects, CapCut, or similar tools.

* Strong attention to detail and an eye for visual quality.

* Ability to follow instructions, incorporate feedback, and meet deadlines.

* Good organizational and communication skills.

* Willingness to learn and follow established editing standards.



What We’re Looking For



* Someone who understands how to make food look appealing through video.

* Someone who values quality over quantity and can maintain consistent editing standards.

* Someone who can identify and correct visual issues before submitting their work.

* Someone who is receptive to feedback and committed to continuous improvement.

* Someone who can work independently while collaborating effectively with the team.



How to Apply



Please submit the following:

1. Your Resume – Include your relevant work experience and editing skills.

2. Portfolio – Share samples of your previous video editing work. Food content or short-form social media videos are preferred.

3. Brief Video Introduction – Submit a short video (approximately 1–2 minutes) introducing yourself. Tell us a little about your background, your video editing experience, the tools you use, and why you’re a good fit for this role.



Important: Applications without a video introduction may not be considered.



We look forward to seeing your work and learning more about you!

title: Long Form Static (LFS) Copywriter – DTC Supplements (Meta Ads)
description:
ABOUT US

We run DTC supplement brands, including pet supplements, and scale them on Meta. Long Form Static ads are one of our main creative formats. We're looking for someone who creates LFS ads that convert, not someone who writes "nice copy".



WHAT YOU'LL DO

Research competitor ads daily and find the angles, hooks and mechanisms that are working.

Work with Claude (AI) to write complete LFS ads: hook, lead, problem, mechanism, failed solutions, proof, week-by-week results, two paths, CTA, PS/PPS.

Create scroll-stopping native images yourself and understand what makes them stop the scroll.

Deliver 1 complete LFS copy plus matching native images every day.

Iterate based on the performance data we share (CTR, hook rate, CPA).



WHAT WE NEED

Experience writing long form static or advertorial-style ads for
/Meta.

Strong understanding of direct response copywriting (awareness levels, mechanism-driven copy, emotional leads).

Experience working with Claude or other AI tools at a high output level. You use AI to work faster, not to skip thinking.

A good eye for native ad images that look organic, not like ads.

Excellent written English, comfortable writing for US customers.

Fast turnaround and open to direct feedback.



NICE TO HAVE

Experience in health, supplements or pet supplements.

Knowledge of what Meta allows in health ads.

Familiar with Foreplay, Atria or Trendtrack.



DETAILS

Full-time remote, long-term.

Paid test task: create one LFS plus native images for one of our products.



HOW TO APPLY

Send us 2–3 LFS ads or native ads you created (include results if you can), a short breakdown (max 150 words) of why an LFS ad you saw recently works, and your expected monthly salary.



Start your application with the word "MECHANISM" so we know you read this. Applications without it will be ignored.

title: Garage Door Operations Manager | Supplier & Purchasing Coordination
description:
We are looking for an experienced Garage Door Operations Manager to manage the daily coordination of door orders, suppliers, purchasing, and installations for a U.S. home services business.



You will take ownership of the process from an approved customer order through purchasing, delivery, installation, and completion. We need someone organized and proactive who can communicate confidently with U.S. suppliers, customers, and technicians and keep multiple jobs moving without constant supervision.



RESPONSIBILITIES

- Communicate with door manufacturers, distributors, and suppliers by phone and
 to obtain quotes, confirm specifications, check stock, and verify lead times.

- Coordinate purchases of garage doors, openers, parts, and installation materials within approved budgets and purchasing procedures.

- Confirm measurements, models, colors, styles, insulation, hardware, and other order details with the field team before submitting supplier orders.

- Prepare and maintain purchase orders, compare supplier quotes, confirm pricing and freight costs, and check order acknowledgments for accuracy.

- Track orders from placement through production, shipment, delivery, or pickup, and follow up proactively on delays and backorders.

- Coordinate supplier deliveries and pickups with technicians and installation schedules so materials are ready when needed.

- Keep customers and team members updated on order status, expected timelines, and scheduling changes.

- Handle damaged, missing, or incorrect items with suppliers and coordinate returns, replacements, warranty claims, and credits.

- Maintain accurate job records, purchasing logs, supplier information, and CRM updates; check supplier invoices against purchase orders and flag discrepancies.

- Manage daily workflows and follow-ups, coordinate team priorities, resolve operational issues, and report outstanding orders, delays, and bottlenecks to ownership.

- Improve purchasing, scheduling, and handoff processes to reduce errors, avoid missed installations, and keep jobs on track.



REQUIRED EXPERIENCE & SKILLS

- Previous operations, purchasing, supplier coordination, or project coordination experience supporting a U.S. business.

- Prior experience in home services, construction, or a related trade, with an understanding of materials, field teams, and job scheduling.

- Strong experience communicating with U.S. customers and business partners. Previous U.S. sales experience is required, including discussing pricing, handling objections, and following up professionally.

- Experience coordinating purchases and tracking orders, delivery dates, and multiple active jobs.

- Management or team coordination experience, with a track record of taking ownership and following tasks through to completion.

- Excellent spoken and written English, strong attention to detail, and confidence speaking with suppliers by phone.

- Ability to read quotes, purchase orders, product specifications, and invoices accurately and resolve discrepancies.

- Experience with CRM or job management software, spreadsheets,
, and online supplier portals.

- Availability during agreed U.S. business hours, reliable internet, a headset, and a quiet workspace.



PREFERRED

- Direct garage door industry experience, including ordering doors, openers, hardware, and replacement parts.

- Familiarity with garage door measurements, configurations, product options, and installation requirements.

- Experience with Jobber, ServiceTitan, Housecall Pro, or similar home services software.



HOW TO APPLY

Please send:

1. Your resume and a brief summary of your U.S. home services, operations, purchasing, and sales experience.

2. Examples of how you have coordinated suppliers, managed orders, or resolved a delivery issue that affected a scheduled job.

3. REQUIRED: A short Loom video introduction explaining your relevant experience and how you would handle a supplier delay when an installation is already scheduled. Include a shareable Loom video link with your application. Applications without a video introduction will not be considered.

4. The systems you have used, your availability during U.S. business hours, and your expected compensation.



Use the subject line: Garage Door Operations Manager.

title: Short form video editor - Female / Fashion preferred
description:
The role

We're hiring a short-form video editor to turn out 5 to 10 polished reels a day for the DTC brands we grow. The format is simple. The bar is not: every reel has to stop the scroll, hold attention and look like it belongs to a premium brand.

Quarters is a growth partner for direct-to-consumer brands. We build the brand, content, infrastructure and paid acquisition behind businesses that are already doing strong revenue. Content is the engine of that system, and you'll be the person keeping it running at volume.

Type: Remote · Hours: [full-time / part-time] · Rate: [to confirm]

What you'll do

• Edit 5 to 10 short-form reels per day for Instagram, TikTok and Meta ads, from raw footage we supply.

• Write and place the hook: pick the strongest opening frame, line or visual so the first 1 to 2 seconds earn the next 10.

• Write on-screen text and captions in sharp, natural English, with no typos and no filler.

• Build clean, editorial layouts: considered typography, framing, spacing and pacing that make a brand look expensive.

• Cut tight. Remove dead air, keep rhythm, and land the message before attention drops.

• Deliver on deadline in the right formats and aspect ratios, organised and named so the team can publish without asking questions.

• Take feedback once and apply it to every edit after.

The style we want

Think fashion editorial, not meme page. The edit should feel calm, confident and premium, and still be impossible to scroll past.

We want

We don't want

Editorial layouts with clean type and deliberate framing

Gimmicky transitions, zooms and whooshes

Restraint: one strong idea per reel

Stacked effects, emojis and sound-effect overload

Pacing that serves the message

Cuts for the sake of cuts

Brand-consistent fonts, colours and spacing

Trendy templates that look like every other account

Hooks built on curiosity, tension or desire

Clickbait that the video doesn't pay off

If your reel would look at home on a premium fashion or wellness brand's feed, you're in the right place.

What you must have

• A portfolio of short-form reels that are highly engaging without relying on tacky editing.

• A deep understanding of hooks. You can explain why a hook works, not just copy one, and you can write several variations for the same video.

• A grasp of the psychology of attention: curiosity gaps, pattern interrupts, social proof, desire, aspiration and tension, and how to use them without cheapening the brand.

• Mastery of English. Native-level spelling, grammar and tone. On-screen copy is part of the edit and has to read perfectly.

• Speed with standards. You can hit 5 to 10 finished reels a day and every one is ready to publish.

• Taste. A clear eye for layout, typography and what makes a brand feel premium.

• Reliability. You hit deadlines, communicate early when something's off, and don't need chasing.

Nice to have

• Experience editing for DTC brands, especially in fashion or health and wellness.

• Experience editing Meta ad creative and an understanding of how organic content and paid ads differ.

• Familiarity with platform metrics such as hook rate, hold rate and watch time, and how editing choices move them.

• Basic motion design for clean text animation and layouts.

How to apply

Send us the following. Applications missing any of these won't be reviewed.

1. A link to your portfolio, with 3 to 5 reels you're proudest of. Fashion or health brand work goes first if you have it.

2. For one of those reels, two or three sentences on why the hook works.

3. How many reels you can realistically deliver per day at your best standard.

4. Your rate and availability.

Shortlisted candidates complete a short paid test: raw footage in, finished reels back within 24 hours. That test is how we d
.

title: Inside Sales Representative – Phone Sales & Closing
description:
ABOUT THE ROLE



We’re looking for a confident Sales Representative who can turn conversations into paying customers. You should have hands-on experience qualifying leads, handling objections, following up, and closing sales over the phone.



If you have worked as an Inside Sales Representative, Telesales Agent, Sales Closer, or outbound sales professional, we encourage you to apply.



KEY RESPONSIBILITIES



- Contact inbound inquiries and outbound prospects through calls,
, and text

- Ask questions to understand customer needs and qualify opportunities

- Explain services, pricing, and value clearly

- Handle objections and confidently ask for the sale

- Follow up consistently with interested prospects and unclosed opportunities

- Close sales and coordinate the next steps with the appropriate team

- Maintain accurate CRM notes, pipeline stages, and follow-up reminders

- Track calls, conversations, conversions, and closed sales

- Work toward agreed sales targets and provide clear progress updates



REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS



- Proven experience in phone sales with personal responsibility for closing deals

- Ability to explain your sales targets, results, and individual contribution

- Strong spoken and written English

- Confident objection handling, negotiation, and closing skills

- Consistent follow-up habits and accurate CRM documentation

- Ability to work independently and respond constructively to coaching

- Availability during U.S. business hours

- Reliable computer, headset, stable internet, and backup connectivity



PREFERRED EXPERIENCE



- Selling to U.S. customers

- Inbound sales, outbound sales, telesales, or inside sales

- Selling services, subscriptions, or recurring plans

- Experience with GoHighLevel, HubSpot, Salesforce, or similar CRMs

- Home services or pest control sales experience



Customer service, upselling, and appointment-setting backgrounds are welcome if you also have direct experience asking for and closing sales.



WHAT WE VALUE



We’re looking for someone who listens carefully, communicates value, follows through, and takes ownership of results. You should be comfortable discussing your sales process and demonstrating your skills in a short interview role-play.



HOW TO APPLY



Send your updated resume using this subject line:



SALES – [Years of Sales Experience] – [Your Name]



Include short answers to these three questions:



1. What did you sell, who were your customers, and did you personally close the sale?

2. What was your sales target, and what results did you achieve? Include the timeframe.

3. Describe a common objection you handled and how you moved the customer toward a purchase.



Please include a 60–90-second voice recording explaining your most relevant sales experience and one deal you personally closed. Avoid sharing confidential customer information.

title: Two video editors needed for two YouTube channels
description:
## Video editors needed for fast-paced YouTube videos — CapCut or Adobe Premiere Pro



Hello!



We’re looking for two experienced video editors to help us create engaging, fast-paced explainer documentaries on YouTube using CapCut or Adobe Premiere Pro.



We’re testing a niche, so this will initially be a trial project. If the niche performs well and we’re happy with the work, we may move to a long-term collaboration.



### What you’ll do



- Edit videos ranging from 20 to 30 minutes.

- Create fast-paced edits with quick cuts, strong timing, and engaging visual sequences.

- Add animations, keyframe movements, camera shakes, warps, transitions, and other visual effects where appropriate.

- Add relevant sound effects and background music 

- Make visual adjustments to improve pacing and keep viewers engaged.

- Follow our editing brief and incorporate specific animations or reference examples that we sometimes provide.

- Deliver polished videos within the agreed deadlines.





### What we’re looking for



- Experience editing in CapCut or Adobe Premiere Pro.

- A portfolio demonstrating fast-paced, engaging video editing.

- Strong animation and keyframing skills.

- A good eye for pacing, timing, and visual storytelling.

- Clear, reliable communication.

- The ability to follow instructions and meet deadlines.

- Availability to **start immediately**.



### Workload and pay



The initial workload will be three videos per week. We’re recruiting two editors and will confirm how the videos will be allocated.



Payment per video:



- 20 minutes — $30 USD

- 25 minutes — $35 USD

- 30 minutes — $40 USD



### Paid trial



Shortlisted applicants will be asked to complete a five-minute trial edit, for which we’ll pay $5 USD.



### How to apply



If this sounds like you, please apply and share relevant samples, particularly fast-paced videos that demonstrate your animation, keyframing, and visual-effects skills. Please also let us know which editing software you use and confirm your availability to start immediately.



We look forward to hearing from you.



Thanks!
